basic_identification.name: Metadata standards (ERC-721, ERC-1155)
basic_identification.originator: William Entriken, Dieter Shirley, Jacob Evans, Nastassia Sachs (ERC-721); Witek Radomski / Enjin (ERC-1155); Ethereum community via EIP process
basic_identification.geography: Global, Ethereum ecosystem. Standards originate from Ethereum Foundation process but adopted worldwide.

core_ideas.core_claim: ERC-721 defines non-fungible token ownership on Ethereum, making each token unique and transferable. ERC-1155 extends this with multi-token contracts supporting both fungible and non-fungible tokens in a single deployment. Together they provide the foundational layer for recording digital art ownership on-chain.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Entirely blockchain-native. These standards define how digital uniqueness is encoded at the smart contract level. The tokenURI/uri pattern for metadata linking is specific to the challenge of associating off-chain content (images, descriptions) with on-chain ownership records. On-chain metadata (Base64-encoded SVG) is unique to fully self-contained digital artifacts.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: The standards themselves are infrastructure-neutral, but their implementation has been deeply captured by attention logic. NFT marketplaces built on these standards optimize for floor price, volume, and trending collections. The metadata structure (name, description, image, attributes/traits) was designed for marketplace display, encouraging visual spectacle and rarity-trait speculation rather than contextual meaning. The 2021-2022 boom demonstrated how these standards enabled attention-driven speculation at massive scale.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Infrastructure-neutral at the protocol level. The standards serve both speculative markets (attention-native) and artist-driven provenance (intention-native) equally. The standards do not inherently favor either, but the ecosystem built on top has been overwhelmingly attention-native. Emerging use of on-chain metadata for generative art (Art Blocks, fxhash) represents a more intention-aligned application.

market_economics.revenue_model: The standards themselves are free and open. Revenue accrues to platforms building on them: primary sale commissions (2.5-10%), secondary royalties (historically 5-10% but now largely unenforced after marketplace royalty wars of 2023), gas fees to validators. ERC-2981 attempted to standardize royalties but enforcement remains voluntary.
market_economics.market_position: Foundational infrastructure. These are the base layer upon which all Ethereum-based NFT markets operate.
market_economics.price_range: N/A for standards themselves. Art sold via ERC-721/1155 ranges from free mints to Beeple's $69.3M sale. Post-crash median NFT prices are below $100.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: The standards are permanent infrastructure and continue growing in deployment. However, NFT trading volume collapsed 93% from Q1 2022 peak ($16.5B) to under $1.1B by Q3 2024. Over 79% of listed NFTs remained unsold in 2024. Despite volume collapse, unique active wallets in dApps grew 485% to 24.6M daily by end of 2024, suggesting the infrastructure is finding non-speculative uses.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Post-crash: shifting from crypto-native speculators toward a mix of digital art collectors, gaming communities, and institutional actors. Traditional art collectors remain a small minority. The speculative demographic has largely exited. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: The standards are self-sustaining as open protocols requiring no ongoing funding. The ecosystem built on them is transitioning from speculative sustainability to utility-based sustainability. On-chain generative art (Art Blocks, fxhash) and gaming represent more durable use cases. The CloneX/RTFKT incident (April 2025, art disappeared when Cloudflare restricted access) exposed how fragile the ecosystem remains when metadata is stored off-chain.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Solidity, Hardhat, Foundry, OpenZeppelin Contracts, IPFS/Pinata/NFT.Storage, Arweave, ethers.js/viem, Remix IDE. Metadata typically stored as JSON conforming to OpenSea metadata standard.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Largely orthogonal. AI-generated art is minted using these same standards without modification. The standards are content-agnostic. The tension around AI art and these standards is social/legal (can AI-generated work be minted and sold as art?) rather than technical. Some projects use on-chain metadata to record whether work was AI-assisted.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Primarily static artifact (token + metadata JSON + media file). ERC-6551 (Token Bound Accounts) introduces dynamic, evolving NFTs that accumulate on-chain history. On-chain generative art uses these standards for real-time/generative output where the code itself is the artwork.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: The vocabulary is heavily market-derived: floor price, traits, rarity, 1/1, editions, PFP, generative, on-chain, metadata. Critical aesthetic vocabulary for the art itself is still forming. The standards encourage attribute-based description (traits with percentage rarity) which flattens aesthetic complexity into market legibility. Publications like Right Click Save and Outland are developing richer critical language.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Open standard (openness), but enclosed ecosystems built on top (OpenSea, Blur). Commons at protocol level, capture at platform level. Infrastructure over spectacle at the standard layer, spectacle-dominant at the marketplace layer. Individual ownership model rather than collective.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Fully open-source. ERC standards are public domain via the Ethereum Improvement Proposal process. OpenZeppelin provides MIT-licensed reference implementations. Anyone can implement without permission or payment.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Ethereum EIP process: community-driven proposal, review by EIP editors, public discussion on Ethereum Magicians forum, rough consensus. No single authority controls the standards. However, marketplace de facto standards (OpenSea metadata schema) are set by corporate actors with outsized influence.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: On-chain token ownership is fully sovereign and portable. However, metadata and media are typically stored off-chain (IPFS, Arweave, or centralized servers), creating dependency and fragility. The CloneX incident demonstrated that art can disappear even while ownership records persist on-chain. Artists cannot easily update metadata after minting on most platforms. The emerging ERC-7572 standard for contract-level metadata improves but does not fully resolve this.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: High interoperability by design. ERC-721 and ERC-1155 are supported by virtually all Ethereum wallets, marketplaces, and tools. Cross-chain bridges extend reach to L2s and other EVM chains. ERC-7572 standardizes contract-level metadata across platforms. However, metadata schemas are not fully standardized beyond OpenSea conventions.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Varies dramatically by implementation. On-chain metadata/art (Base64-encoded): permanent as long as Ethereum exists. IPFS-pinned: depends on pinning services continuing. Arweave: designed for permanence (pay-once model). Centralized server: at-risk, as proven by CloneX. No standard mandates a specific preservation approach.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Absent at the standard level. ERC-721/1155 define ownership transfer mechanics but have no built-in consent layer for how the underlying content may be used, reproduced, or trained upon. The approve/transferFrom pattern handles transfer consent but not usage consent. IP rights are entirely off-chain and unenforceable by the protocol.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Initially parallel, now partially absorbed. Major auction houses (Christie's, Sotheby's, Phillips) have conducted NFT sales using these standards. Art Basel and major fairs include digital art sections. However, many traditional institutions remain skeptical, and the post-crash period has cooled institutional interest. The standards serve as a bridge between crypto-native and traditional art markets.
field_position.what_it_enables: Verifiable digital ownership without intermediaries. Programmable royalties (though unenforced). Provenance tracking on an immutable ledger. Global 24/7 markets for digital art. On-chain generative art where the algorithm is the artwork. Fractional ownership via ERC-1155. Token-gated experiences and communities.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Rich metadata standards for meaning, context, and artistic intent beyond marketplace display. Enforceable royalty mechanisms. Built-in content licensing or usage rights. Preservation guarantees for off-chain content. Consent architecture. Support for evolving or relational artworks. Machine-readable provenance of meaning (not just ownership). The metadata schema (name, description, image, attributes) is impoverished relative to art historical documentation needs.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists without crypto literacy or technical skills to mint. People in jurisdictions where crypto is restricted or banned. Artists who cannot afford gas fees (partially addressed by L2s). Collectors without crypto wallets. The elderly and less technically literate. Communities without reliable internet access. Artists whose practice does not fit the single-artifact model (performance, relational, collaborative work).
field_position.frontier_signal: Established at the core standard level. Frontier at the extension level: ERC-6551 (Token Bound Accounts), ERC-7572 (contract-level metadata), ERC-404 (hybrid fungible/non-fungible), and on-chain metadata patterns represent active innovation. The challenge to marketplace-centric metadata schemas is emerging.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Marketplace algorithms (OpenSea trending, Blur analytics), social media (Twitter/X crypto art community), curated platforms (Art Blocks, fxhash), word of mouth in Discord communities, institutional exhibitions. Discovery is heavily platform-mediated.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: The standards themselves have zero attention dependency as protocol-level infrastructure. The ecosystem built on them is highly attention-dependent: marketplace rankings, Twitter virality, Discord community engagement. If social media disappeared, the standards would persist but the market activity would collapse.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: The standards are intention-neutral infrastructure. They could serve a field-intelligence system as easily as a speculative marketplace. Currently, the dominant use is attention-native (marketplace optimization). Emerging intention-aligned uses include on-chain generative art archiving, verifiable digital certificates, and provenance tracking for conservation.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Strong commons contribution at the standard level: open EIPs, open-source implementations, shared metadata conventions. The ecosystem built on top has been more extractive: proprietary marketplace algorithms, walled-garden curation, enclosed analytics. The open standard enables commons but does not guarantee it.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Ownership only. These standards track who owns a token and its transfer history. They do not track provenance of meaning, interpretation, exhibition history, or contextual evolution. Metadata is typically static after minting.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Archival at the ownership level (immutable chain of transfers). Static for metadata (no built-in mechanism for temporal evolution of meaning). ERC-6551 introduces accumulative temporal logic where NFTs build on-chain history over time.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not address absence. The standards record what exists on-chain but have no mechanism for representing what is missing: lost context, broken metadata links, disappeared media, unrecorded exhibition history, or gaps in provenance. The CloneX incident revealed this gap dramatically.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Consensus-seeking at the technical standard level (EIP process seeks rough consensus). Neither coherence nor consensus at the meaning level: the standards make no claim about what constitutes art, value, or significance. They enable multiple incompatible value systems to coexist on the same infrastructure.
coherence.contestability: Technically high: anyone can propose competing standards via the EIP process. Practically constrained: marketplace adoption creates lock-in. If OpenSea supports a standard, it becomes dominant regardless of technical merit. The royalty wars of 2023 showed how marketplace power can override standard intentions (ERC-2981 royalties made optional).
coherence.forkability: Fully forkable. The standards are open and can be forked, extended, or reimplemented on any EVM chain. Practical barriers include network effects (Ethereum mainnet liquidity), marketplace support, and community adoption. Numerous L2 chains and alternative blockchains have forked these standards successfully.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The open standard approach: building shared, forkable infrastructure that anyone can implement. The EIP governance process as a model for community-driven standard evolution. The principle that ownership records should be immutable and verifiable. The interoperability mandate: any system built on these standards can talk to any other. The lesson from on-chain metadata: critical information should not depend on external services.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The impoverished metadata model that reduces art to marketplace attributes (name, description, image, traits). The ownership-only provenance model that ignores meaning, context, and interpretation. The implicit assumption that digital art is a static artifact to be owned rather than a living practice to be understood. The gas-fee barrier model that excludes participation by cost. The marketplace-driven standard adoption that gives corporate platforms veto power over protocol evolution.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: ERC-721/1155 solved ownership provenance but ignored meaning provenance. A(DAI) is building the meaning layer that these standards structurally lack. The tension is productive: A(DAI) can build on top of the ownership infrastructure while adding the contextual, relational, and temporal metadata that these standards cannot carry. The challenge is that the existing ecosystem has trained users to think of metadata as marketplace display rather than knowledge infrastructure.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Increasing. The EU MiCA regulation classifies some NFTs as crypto-assets subject to disclosure requirements. The SEC has signaled that some NFTs may be securities. The EU AI Act does not directly apply to token standards but affects AI-generated content minted as NFTs. Copyright law remains unsettled regarding what rights transfer with an NFT sale. The Howey test may apply to fractionalized NFTs or those sold with promises of profit.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Varies by implementation. Most NFT projects retain copyright with the creator and grant limited display licenses to buyers. Some (CC0 projects like Nouns) place work in the public domain. Bored Ape Yacht Club granted commercial rights to holders. There is no standard IP model embedded in the token standards themselves; IP terms are handled off-chain and are often ambiguous.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in for participation (must actively mint/buy). No consent mechanism for how underlying content is used by third parties, AI training, or derivative works. The standards have no built-in opt-in or opt-out for any usage beyond ownership transfer.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Dependent on Ethereum (or EVM-compatible chains) for the base layer. Dependent on IPFS/Arweave/centralized servers for metadata storage. Dependent on marketplaces (OpenSea, Blur, Foundation) for price discovery and trading. Single points of failure exist at the metadata storage and marketplace layers but not at the standard/protocol layer.
ecosystem.network_effects: Massive network effects. ERC-721 is the dominant NFT standard with near-universal wallet and marketplace support. This creates a strong moat against competing standards. ERC-1155 benefits from the same ecosystem. New standards (ERC-6551, ERC-7572) must be backward-compatible to gain adoption.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: The standards are permanent infrastructure unaffected by market cycles. The ecosystem using them experienced severe decline (93% volume drop) but is stabilizing around utility use cases: gaming NFTs, digital identity, on-chain generative art, and real-world asset tokenization. The speculative PFP market has largely collapsed. Growth areas include L2 adoption, lower gas costs enabling micro-transactions, and integration with traditional platforms (GoDaddy, Coinbase).
